svg.text: D-D SOCK ARM — a cheap cobot in an inflated, leak-tested sleeve
A bought six-axis arm hangs from the ceiling inside one seamless silicone sleeve kept at +5 mbar: the wet cell holds one smooth object.
cell 900 × 520 × 650 · FR3-class arm, 622 mm reach, 3 kg
sleeve 0.8 mm platinum silicone, ≈ 0.5 m²
lever knife 3:1: 30 N at the handle → ≈ 90 N
8 axes (6 bought, with F/T sensing) · 0 dynamic seals
parts ≈ 7–9 k€
FRONT VIEW of the cell
ceiling flange Ø160, clamp ring, dry-air feed
box dock
pot
board 400 × 300 on a trunnion; spray bar below
base + sleeve clamp

g.text: the arm pours: no tip bar needed

svg.text: fixed nozzles
sleeve pressure
The board is a "third hand": V-groove,
fulcrum eye, spike row, ice-chuck patch.
Natural for this arm: flip, pour, toss,
ladle, baste — and plating nicely.
Peeling: blade kept normal to an uneven
potato under force control.
weak points: sleeve fatigue at the elbow
(10⁵–10⁶ flexes a year) and knife nicks;
622 mm reach sweeps more than 520 deep;
only 30 N; hardest software of all five

g.text: 1/5 The whole arm sits in one seamless sleeve at +5 mbar: folds are blown smooth and any leak blows outwards.
2/5 Lever knife: its tip hooks into a fulcrum eye on the board, so a 3 kg arm presses the handle and cuts carrots.
3/5 With roll and tilt in the wrist the arm lifts a box and pours it into the pot itself.
4/5 After an ingredient change the board flips face-down on its trunnion over a spray bar.
5/5 "Shower dance": at +15 mbar the arm runs poses that open each joint's folds towards fixed nozzles.
